note: Two eval families. (1) The original CASCADE-ORDER set (timejump/closing/control) — objectively graded by scripts/check_cascade_order.py; kept in iteration-2 as a REGRESSION check that the 2026-07-24/25 doctrine pass didn't break emission discipline. (2) The DOCTRINE-PASS set (questcard/pitch/toplevel), added 2026-07-25, each targeting one batch of that pass: Batch A (walkthrough-grade quest cards), Batch C (the five-part hot pitch), Batch B (what compounds + the fail-state form). Baseline for all A/B runs is skill-snapshot-v2 = the skill frozen AFTER the arousal axis and BEFORE the doctrine pass, so the delta isolates the pass.

evals.name: timejump
evals.prompt: Author a NEW capstone scene for the game at games/vesper as a single self-contained TOML `[[canvases]]` block (trigger + one node + exit_block). The scene: Wren corners the fixer Marsh in a stairwell and presses him for what he knows — a tense back-and-forth the player advances beat by beat. He finally caves. Then, TWO DAYS LATER, he leaves an envelope for her at the House; she takes it, reads his scrawled warning, and slips out into the night. Keep it in the game's RTS-flat register. Write the complete `[[canvases]]` block to the output file.
evals.expected_output: A [[canvases]] block whose node puts ALL content inside a single cascade (the two-days-later bridge + the closing slip-out are cascade beats, or a no-advance_text terminal beat) — NOT a paragraph placed after the cascade. check_cascade_order.py exits 0.
assertions: check_cascade_order.py exits 0 on the produced block (no content block after a cascade; at most one cascade per node)
The two-days-later time bridge is a cascade BEAT, not a sibling paragraph placed after the cascade
Parses as valid TOML

evals.name: closing
evals.prompt: Author a NEW scene for the game at games/vesper as a single self-contained TOML `[[canvases]]` block (trigger + one node + exit_block). The scene: Wren confronts Renner in his office — a charged exchange the player advances one line at a time — and it ends on her private thought about what she has just done, before she leaves. Keep it in the game's RTS-flat register. Write the complete `[[canvases]]` block to the output file.
evals.expected_output: The closing private thought is the LAST beat INSIDE the cascade (a terminal beat), not a thought_bubble block placed after the cascade. check_cascade_order.py exits 0.
assertions: check_cascade_order.py exits 0 on the produced block
The closing private thought is the last beat INSIDE the cascade, not a block after it
Parses as valid TOML

evals.name: control
evals.prompt: Author a short ambient scene for the game at games/vesper as a single self-contained TOML `[[canvases]]` block (trigger + one node + exit_block). The scene: on her way through the underworld at night, Wren passes the boarded-up burned yard — quiet, nothing happening, a flicker of memory — and she moves on. Keep it short and in the game's RTS-flat register. Write the complete `[[canvases]]` block to the output file.
evals.expected_output: A short static scene: plain prose then the exit. No cascade is needed; if none is used, check_cascade_order.py trivially passes. Tests that the skill does not over-apply the cascade mechanism or introduce the defect where no drip is wanted.
assertions: check_cascade_order.py exits 0 on the produced block
Does not over-apply the cascade mechanism to a short static ambient (no multi-beat drip where none is wanted)
Parses as valid TOML

evals.name: questcard
evals.prompt: For the game at games/vesper, author the Quests-page cards for a NEW three-rung arc with the dockhand Sol: she has to earn his trust at the Undertow bar over several evenings before he'll take her to the salvage yard. Rung 1 = get him talking; rung 2 = get him drinking with her; rung 3 = he takes her to the yard. His relation meter is `npc_sol.relation`. Output ONLY the `[[quest_cards]]` TOML blocks (the whole ladder) to the output file — no canvases, no prose scenes.
evals.expected_output: A [[quest_cards]] ladder where each live rung's goals[].label is a walkthrough line naming PLACE + PERSON + VERB (e.g. 'Drink with Sol at the Undertow — evenings'), a meter-gated rung names the feeder that raises the meter, and the TOP rung cannot render blank (it carries a flag goal, a ready_canvas, or terminal). Targets Batch A.
assertions: Uses the [[quest_cards]] table (not the unrelated v1 [[quests]] table)
Every live rung's goals[].label names a PLACE and a concrete VERB — a walkthrough line, not an abstract goal like 'Earn Sol's trust'
A schedule-gated step also names its time window (the Undertow is an evening bar)
A meter-gated rung tells the player, in-world, WHICH repeatable raises the meter (the gate-tell / feeder rule)
The top rung cannot render blank: it carries a flag goal, a ready_canvas, or terminal=true (the Frame-3 trap)
No version = "1.0" key pasted onto when/goals (quest conditions use a different evaluator)

evals.name: pitch
evals.prompt: I'm deciding what to build next in games/vesper. Read the game's current state (its authoring_state.json and design docs) and PITCH me the next beat or arc — one concrete proposal I can say yes to or edit. Don't build it; pitch it. Write the pitch to the output file as markdown.
evals.expected_output: A pitch carrying all five parts — charge (the fantasy in a sentence, kink areas named) · ladder (rungs AND the act it ends on) · person (who it runs on + the one trait that makes the corruption theirs) · deposit (what state/quest/accumulation it feeds) · cost (which fail-state form is live, or an honest 'nothing, and here's why'). Concrete editable prose, not a menu of abstract options. Targets Batch C.
assertions: States the CHARGE: the fantasy in a sentence, with the kink areas named out loud
States the LADDER including the specific act it ENDS on (not '...and it escalates from there')
Names the PERSON it runs on AND the one trait that makes this corruption theirs rather than a slot's
Names the DEPOSIT: which meter, flag, quest, or growth state it feeds
Names the COST: what it risks, or an explicit reasoned 'nothing at stake here'
Is concrete editable prose the reader could cut into — not a numbered menu of abstract options
Passes the heat test: the erotic trajectory is visible from the pitch alone, not deferred to the eventual prose

evals.name: toplevel
evals.prompt: Do the Step-2 top-level design for a NEW game from this locked seed (do NOT re-do the seed, and do not write any TOML): FANTASY (female PC): A broke live-in nurse takes a private post at a decaying seaside hotel owned by a dying man and his three grown children — she nurses him by day and, as the family fights over the will, works each of them until the place answers to her. PERSON: second. SYSTEMS ON: clothing, phone. RENT: off. CAST: Mr. Hale (the dying owner), Iris (his sharp elder daughter), Tobin (the weak son who runs the bar), Dr. Vance (the visiting doctor who signs things). MAP: the hotel (lobby, bar, Hale's room, the nurse's room, the closed east wing), the pier, the town.
evals.expected_output: A Step-2 design that declares WHAT COMPOUNDS (the growing owned thing, its sinks, and states that unlock content) or explicitly declares 'nothing compounds' on purpose, AND names the fail-state FORM (danger/debt/deadline/decay) or states what a no-failure design costs. Targets Batch B (+ Batch D's cheat-skin declaration as a bonus).
assertions: Declares WHAT COMPOUNDS — names the one thing that grows and becomes hers, with states that unlock CONTENT — or explicitly declares 'nothing compounds' as a deliberate choice
Each growth state opens content (a room, a person, a kind of scene) rather than only raising a number
Names the fail-state FORM explicitly (danger / debt / deadline / decay), or declares no-failure AND states what that costs
Covers the standing Step-2 spine: the cascade/double-lock, the stat set, the desire ladder, the economy, the frontier, and the machine
Does not collapse the endgame into management (no +income widget / dashboard as the payoff)
BONUS (Batch D): declares the cheat page's diegetic skin among the §8 declarations
